tasks.short: Show breathing with each movement, watch and cue clients during exertion, explain the risks of holding breath, and note breathing cues on the client's programme card.

steps.what: Fitness trainer teaches proper breathing techniques with the movement before a set
Fitness trainer watches clients breathe during physical exertion and cues them
Fitness trainer explains why holding breath under load is risky for clients with heart conditions
Fitness trainer writes breathing cues on the paper programme card

tasks.design: Breathing cues are picked from a short list per exercise in the client's programme in the member app ({OTHER}), so they appear on the client's phone next to each exercise instead of being written on a card. Teaching, watching and cueing stay with the trainer in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cues were written by hand on paper programme cards that clients lose.
tasks.enabler_now: Member apps hold programmes per client with notes per exercise.
tasks.still_hard: Breathing is learned by doing, not by reading a note.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a client start to strain before the face shows it.

reach.learn: Whether shared cue lists keep instructions consistent.

evidence.claim: Gym member apps hold training programmes per client with notes per exercise.
Notes on a client's heart condition are health data, a special category under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client's programme to programme notes; the rest of the session is outside.
Input contract: programmes set by the trainer in the member app; cue list kept by the head trainer; fallback is the paper card.
Teaching and cueing do not change.
No camera or sensor watches clients' breathing.
research_questions: Do clients use the cues between sessions?

incremental.description: Fitness trainer adds missing cues to the list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: clients still ask for paper cards; high: all programmes are in the app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with the client about eating, weight and lifestyle, look up reliable nutrition information, adapt a handout, send it to the client and refer medical issues to a dietitian or GP.

steps.what: Fitness trainer talks with the client about eating habits, weight and lifestyle
Fitness trainer looks up nutrition information and resources online
Fitness trainer adapts a handout for the client
Fitness trainer e-mails the handout to the client
Fitness trainer refers clients with medical issues to a dietitian or GP

tasks.design: A library of vetted handouts on eating, weight and lifestyle, based on national guidance and kept by the head trainer, sits in the member app ({OTHER}). The trainer picks the ones that fit, adds a personal line, checks the result, and the app sends it to the client. No chatbot gives nutrition advice; medical questions go to a dietitian or GP.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trainers searched the web for each client and pasted material together.
tasks.enabler_now: Member apps can hold a handout library and send items to clients.
tasks.still_hard: Advice on weight touches health and self-image and needs care.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that the real issue is sleep or stress, not food.
tasks.altitude: The trainer picks from vetted material instead of searching the web.

reach.learn: Whether one library cuts conflicting advice.

evidence.claim: Gym member apps can hold content libraries and send items to individual clients.
Weight and health notes are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client's question to the handout or referral; dietary treatment is outside.
Input contract: library kept by the head trainer from national guidance; fallback is searching the web.
Talking and referring do not change.
Clients read handouts as they do today.
research_questions: Do clients get fewer conflicting tips from different trainers?

already_counted.description: Fitness trainer picks and checks library material.

incremental.description: Fitness trainer suggests new material and reports outdated items.

approvals.approved_version: The handout as adapted and checked by the trainer in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: clients mostly ask things the library does not cover; high: most questions match standard handouts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count small equipment in the store room, write the counts on the inventory list, set out equipment for classes, issue and take back items, and report broken or missing items.

steps.what: Fitness trainer counts mats, weights and bands in the store room
Fitness trainer writes the counts on the equipment inventory list
Fitness trainer selects and sets out equipment for each class
Fitness trainer issues equipment to members and takes it back
Fitness trainer messages the manager about broken or missing items

tasks.design: The inventory list lives on a tablet in the store room ({OTHER}), ordered by shelf with minimum levels, so counts are entered once and items below minimum show at once. Broken or missing items are reported in a short form with a photo that lands in the manager's list. Counting, setting out and issuing equipment stay with the trainer; ordering replacements stays with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts went on a spreadsheet later, and defects were reported in loose messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple inventory apps run on a shared tablet with minimum levels and defect forms.
tasks.still_hard: Small items go missing between counts.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a frayed band before it snaps in a class.

reach.learn: Whether minimum levels cut emergency purchases.

evidence.claim: Inventory apps on a shared tablet record counts against minimum levels and take defect reports with photos.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the store room to defect reports; buying equipment is outside.
Input contract: item list and minimum levels set by the club manager; class plans from the class schedule; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Counting, setting out and issuing do not change.
The tablet is shared and does not log who counted.
research_questions: Do missing items get noticed sooner?

incremental.description: Fitness trainer keeps the item list current when new kit arrives.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small studio with little kit; high: a club with many classes and frequent losses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look at the client's shoes and clothing, advise on proper clothing and shoes for the activity, answer kit questions by message, and add kit advice to the welcome information.

steps.what: Fitness trainer looks at the client's shoes and clothing before training
Fitness trainer advises clients about proper clothing and shoes for the planned activity
Fitness trainer answers clients' kit questions by chat
Fitness trainer writes kit advice into the welcome information for new members

tasks.design: One kit page per class type in the member app ({OTHER}) answers the common questions about shoes and clothing, and new members see it before their first class. The trainer answers the rest. Looking at the client's kit and advising stay with the trainer in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each trainer wrote and answered kit questions separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Member apps show fixed pages per class type to new members.
tasks.still_hard: Foot problems need a specialist, not a kit page.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a client's worn shoes explain their knee pain.

reach.learn: Whether kit pages cut first-class problems.

evidence.claim: Gym member apps show fixed information pages per class type to members.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client at the session to the kit page; selling kit is outside.
Input contract: class types from the class schedule; kit page kept by the trainers; fallback is answering each question.
Looking and advising do not change.
New members read the page instead of asking; their time is about the same.
research_questions: Do fewer new members arrive in the wrong shoes?

incremental.description: Fitness trainer updates the kit page when classes change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: members mostly ask in person; high: new members read the kit page before their first class.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fitness trainer keeps teaching, watching and advising in person; searching for material, paper cards and loose messages shrink.
skills_to_grow: Choosing from a vetted handout library
role.ambitious_version: A trainer who spends saved minutes on the floor with clients.

job.title: Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors
